children.funFact: Tropicbirds perform dramatic courtship displays called 'back-to-back flights' where pairs fly in synchronized patterns while calling loudly, showing off their elegant tail streamers to potential mates.

children.description: Tropicbirds are elegant seabirds with long, streaming tail feathers and brilliant white plumage. They are skilled ocean fliers that spend most of their lives far from shore, diving from great heights to catch fish and squid in tropical and subtropical waters.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Tropicbirds are easily recognized by their distinctive long tail streamers that can be twice the length of their body, along with their pointed wings and bills perfectly adapted for plunge-diving.
children.funFact: Despite being called tropicbirds, they occasionally get blown far off course by storms and can show up as rare visitors to New England waters, much to the excitement of local birdwatchers.

children.description: Tropicbirds are elegant seabirds with long, streaming tail feathers and pointed wings built for life over the open ocean. They are skilled divers that plunge from great heights to catch fish and squid in tropical and subtropical waters around the world.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Tropicbirds are easily recognized by their distinctive long tail streamers, bright white plumage with black markings, and dagger-like bills. Unlike other seabirds, they have all four toes connected by webbing.
children.funFact: When tropicbirds dive for fish, they can plunge into the ocean from heights of up to 100 feet, hitting the water at speeds of nearly 40 mph.

children.name: Ciconiiformes
Ciconiidae
Mycteria
children.description: Mycteria storks are large wading birds with distinctive thick, heavy bills that curve slightly downward at the tip. These impressive birds are built for life in wetlands, with long legs for wading through shallow water and keen eyesight for spotting fish and other aquatic prey. They're known for their patient hunting style, often standing motionless before striking with lightning speed.
children.distinguishingFeatures: What sets Mycteria storks apart from other stork species is their unique bill shape - thick and heavy with a distinctive downward curve at the tip, perfectly designed for their specialized feeding technique. Unlike many other storks, they also have a distinctive bare, dark-colored head and neck in adults.
children.funFact: Wood Storks are the only storks native to North America and have one of the most sensitive bills in the bird world - they can snap their bill shut in just 25 milliseconds when they feel a fish touch it!

children.description: Storks are large, long-legged wading birds known for their impressive size and distinctive appearance. They have long necks, long pointed bills, and broad wings that make them excellent soaring birds. Most species are found in wetlands where they hunt for fish, frogs, and other aquatic prey.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Storks are distinguished from herons and other wading birds by their straight, heavy bills and their habit of flying with neck extended rather than pulled back. They also lack the powder down feathers that herons use for cleaning.
children.funFact: Storks are nearly voiceless birds that communicate primarily through bill clattering, creating loud rattling sounds by rapidly opening and closing their beaks.

children.description: Storks are large, long-legged wading birds that belong to the order Ciconiiformes. These impressive birds are characterized by their tall stature, long necks, and distinctive long, pointed bills that they use to catch fish, frogs, and other aquatic prey in shallow waters.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Storks are distinguished from other wading birds by their straight, dagger-like bills and their habit of flying with their necks extended forward rather than folded back like herons.
children.funFact: Despite the popular myth about storks delivering babies, these birds are actually silent flyers due to their broad wings, and they communicate primarily through bill-clattering rather than vocalizations.
